Structural to the FFI boundary. proven's verified core is Idris2/Zig; every binding must cross from a foreign runtime into it, and that crossing is unsafe by construction in the host language — the guarantee holds on the core's side of the boundary, not on the caller's. This is an ARCHITECTURAL exemption, not deferred work: it does not shrink over time and there is no version of these bindings without it. Findings in the verified core itself are NOT covered here and are listed individually below.

Provably true, but not visible to the totality checker. In `tokenize`, the branch is guarded by `isDigit c`, so `span isDigit cs` consumes at least one character and `rest` is strictly shorter than `cs`. `span` returns `(List a, List a)` with no type-level relation to its input, so Idris2 cannot see the decrease. Discharge by threading a fuel bound or by a `span` that returns a proof its second component is a suffix — NOT by leaving the assertion unexamined, since an unchecked `assert_smaller` in a library promising termination is a hole in the central guarantee.

Verified by reading each site 2026-08-06. Listed per-file rather than by a `**/*.idr` pattern on purpose: a pattern would blind this repository to a real secret in any future Idris file. Upstream fix belongs in the Hypatia rule, which should not match inside comments.
